rows.b: A brass box where numbered wheels are turned with a stylus to add and subtract. Carry from one wheel to the next happens automatically inside the gearing.
A compact machine with a round cathode-ray display and a light pen, sold to labs that wanted hands-on computing. Programmers wrote the first video game, Spacewar!, on it.
A machine the size of a small refrigerator that a single department could afford and keep. It sold by the tens of thousands and carried computing into labs and factories.
A material that flips between glassy and crystalline states to store bits, and can do arithmetic in the flip itself. It bridges memory and processor.
A future machine that does exascale arithmetic with photons instead of electrons, in chips of waveguides and modulators. SPECULATION: no such complete machine exists.
Qubits carried by single particles of light race through chips of waveguides and detectors. Photons barely interact with noise, and the chips can work closer to room temperature.
Light waves squeezed along metal surfaces carry signals in spaces far smaller than a wavelength. It promises optics at electronic sizes.
